influences.name: Edgar
influences.context: In Tangerine Dream we have ideas and sonic guideposts from Edgar and a very good team when it comes to combine sounds.

influences.name: Ulrich
influences.context: Ulrich is unbelievably good at creating shimmering and airy sounds – meanwhile I'm used to making huge and bassy sounds, and catchy melodies.

influences.name: J.S. Bach
influences.context: during my training as an organist in Delmenhorst, I had become acquainted with the music of old masters, baroque compositions by Italian composers and, of course, the fugues and preludes of J.S. Bach

influences.name: Gustav Mahler
influences.context: I listen to classical composers such as Gustav Mahler, whose movements of a symphony last more than 40 minutes or longer and sound as one

influences.name: Kurt Ader
influences.context: I met Kurt in June 2017 at the electronic festival Synthfest in Nantes. Here he introduced me to his sound design specifically for the Korg Kronos 2 workstation, as well as his KApro Sound Libraries... So inspiring were Kurt's sounds for me that I was able to finish this album so quickly

influences.name: Christoph Franke
influences.context: this piece reminds me of the performance, how Christoph Franke and I during my time with Tangerine Dream had produced this music in his studio in Berlin-Spandau, in a night session around 1982. Each of us knew exactly what to do, each had shared his talent with the other without much explanation or discussion.
